messages:
Anya V: Thanks for the all-hands. Quick follow-up: what's the current runway assumption used in slides (months) and are we moving any spend from OPEX -> CAPEX this quarter? Also, procurement approval flow when >$50k? :raising_hand:
Mike (Finance): Hey Anya — runway in slides is 13 months at current burn; scenario table had 11/13/16 depending on hiring pace. We should clarify which scenario the product roadmap maps to.
Olivia (CEO): We intentionally showed the conservative 11-month plan for leadership ops questions; hiring ramp targets the 13-mo baseline if hiring slows. We'll publish a clarified slide later today.
Raj (Eng): For projects we've been asked to treat GPUs as OPEX vs CAPEX depending on contract. Can finance confirm preferred accounting treatment for Dedicated infra purchases?
Mike (Finance): Good q. Short answer: short-term reserved cloud commit (monthly/annual) = OPEX. Hardware purchases / appliance installs (on-prem racks) = CAPEX. If it's a multi-year support contract with capitalizable hardware, we can talk to accounting. cc: @Kate (People Ops) for headcount treatment on the scenario.
Kate (People Ops): Headcount modeled as FTE OPEX. For hiring freeze triggers, we use a monthly burn threshold and slide-deck scenario — HR will pause external req approvals if we enter the lower runway band.
procurement-bot: FYI — procurement approvals: 
```
<$PROCURE_FORM|procurement form> -> vendor security review (if external) -> PO request -> Finance approval if > $50,000 -> Legal signoff if > $100,000
```
Mike (Finance): To be precise: our gate thresholds are: approvals needed for spend >= `25,000` (manager+finance), `50,000` (director+finance), `100,000` (director+legal+finance). We can adjust if product teams need fast lanes.
Anya V: Thanks — could someone post the updated slide and a clear checklist for procurement fast lanes? Many teams asked for a short checklist during AH.
Mike (Finance): Will do. I'll post updated slides and a 1-page FAQ within 4 hours. If teams have imminently queued purchases, DM me or tag `#procurement` and we'll triage prioritization.
Raj (Eng): If we need to move an existing Dedicated pool from cloud to on-prem (capex), what's the lead time and who signs off?
Mike (Finance): That would be 8-12 weeks for procurement + onboarding, and needs Finance+Infra+EngDirector signoff. Please open a ticket in `#eng-infra` with cost estimate and rough SOW.
Olivia (CEO): High level: our priority is preserving runway. If moving to CAPEX materially reduces 12-mo ops cost, it will be considered, but not if it increases near-term cash burn.
Anya V: Great, thanks everyone. If I don't hear back about the checklist I'll ping Mike later today. :thumbsup:
